headings: # Before You Try to Go Deep
## Your Body Might Need Some Love First

rows.label: 97.1 A: cut Bringing the challenge back
rows.start: And what about those hard dreams, or images that pop up duri

beside.label: Before the cut
beside.text: Bring the challenge back gradually, and only when you want to and you're recovering well. Some people try to toughen themselves up in a cauldron, but what you're looking for is the edge where you can actually learn. And what about those hard dreams, or images that pop up during a session? They can show what feels important or frightening right now. Sometimes they show what feels missing, or what feels needed. They aren't evidence that what you saw in them happened, though, and shouldn't be used to confirm a memory or rebuild one. Or to suggest one.

headings: # Before You Try to Go Deep
## You Don’t Need an Inner Monologue

rows.label: 98.1 A: cut "That's ok, too."
rows.start: And it might not be the same order all the time. You could h

beside.label: Before the cut
beside.text: And it might not be the same order all the time. You could have a feeling before thoughts, or thoughts might come first and provoke a feeling. They say hindsight is 20/20, but you actually might not even know which happened first. That's ok, too.

headings: # Building Trust With Your Little One
## Not Every Hero Wears A Cape

rows.label: 98.2 A: cut "It doesn't mean failure."
rows.start: After the day, look at what actually happened. If you did th

beside.label: Before the cut
beside.text: After the day, look at what actually happened. If you did the Protector action(s), not feeling better right away is information to learn from. It doesn't mean failure. Healing is nonlinear, and sometimes standing up for yourself might make you feel worse at first. Not doing it is harder to figure out. Fear is the first guess, but maybe you didn't know how or why. Being worn out can stop you too, and sometimes whoever said they'd help couldn't make it. Hey, we've all been there. 🤗

headings: # Building Trust With Your Little One
## Love Doesn't Have to Wait for Trust ❤️
### Instead of Blame

rows.label: 98.3 A: cut "You still did what you did, though"
rows.start: Whichever age it picks on, saving everybody was never your j

beside.label: Before the cut
beside.text: Whichever age it picks on, saving everybody was never your job. At fifteen you probably didn't even have your own money, or anywhere else to go. And actually, not to beat a dead horse here, but every age of you was stuck with whatever it had then, even the adult you were last year. Hindsight being 20/20 doesn't change that. You still did what you did, though, and if it hurt people or damaged a life, that may need repair.

rows.label: 98.4 A: cut "Feeling calmer doesn't mean their complaint is wrong"
rows.start: If your stomach tightens while your little one waits for an

beside.label: Before the cut
beside.text: If your stomach tightens while your little one waits for an answer, slower exhales may help you stay with them. Feeling calmer doesn't mean their complaint is wrong, though, and it won't make them trust you on its own.

headings: # Simple Practices
## Catch the Hook Before the Story Takes Over

rows.label: 97.2 A: cut "If nobody is in danger"
rows.start: When you catch it, look around and just take a moment to enj

beside.label: Before the cut
beside.text: When you catch it, look around and just take a moment to enjoy some free honesty: "Oh! I'm hooked again! That's awesome I could notice it!" If nobody is in danger, take a breath or three before you finish whatever you were doing. Sometimes human beings need to be being, not always doing. 🙃 Maybe then you'll find there's enough adult around to be nice to your little boo for a second. Or enough Protector to stop something you'd regret later.

rows.label: 97.3 A: cut The danger-or-doctor add-on to your touch example
rows.start: The opposite extreme of our pendulum, throwing everything tr

beside.label: Before the cut
beside.text: The opposite extreme of our pendulum, throwing everything transient away, as some people do with "thought-noting" practice, also isn't healthy, except as a meditation exercise. Transient feelings and thoughts can be meaningful signals. For example, if you don't want to be touched, say no now and work out what it means later. Same if something might be dangerous right now, or might be a medical warning sign: step away or get checked first.

headings: # Simple Practices
## Journal With Each Hand

rows.label: 98.5 A: cut "(nothing made up)"
rows.start: Lucia Capacchione, an art therapist, wrote a whole book on t

beside.label: Before the cut
beside.text: Lucia Capacchione, an art therapist, wrote a whole book on this one, [The Power of Your Other Hand](https://www.luciac.com/). As titles go, it's pretty literal. Your other hand, the clumsy one, writes like a first grader anyway, so it gets the scared or hurt feelings (nothing made up). The usual hand answers, as the grown-up. Some people who get nothing but silence from their little one are surprised by what the other hand comes up with. A protective part might grab the pen first, and then it gets that hand until it's had its say.

headings: # Simple Practices
## Just Like Me

rows.label: 97.4 A: cut "Getting in touch is a separate decision"
rows.start: If you've tried Pema Chödrön's

beside.label: Before the cut
beside.text: If you've tried Pema Chödrön's [tonglen](https://www.lionsroar.com/how-to-practice-tonglen-meditation/), this is a gentler cousin, and normal breathing is fine. Whoever hurt you might come to mind, too. I'd leave out forgiving them and picturing their childhood. Getting in touch is a separate decision, for a much calmer day.

headings: # Simple Practices
## “And So That’s the Way It Happened!”

rows.label: 98.6 A: cut "And nobody's off the hook"
rows.start: Does saying it make the memory fiction? Well, no, it's still

beside.label: Before the cut
beside.text: Does saying it make the memory fiction? Well, no, it's still what happened, as far as you remember it, even if some details turn out fuzzy. And nobody's off the hook (you included, if you were the one who did the harm): whatever repair is owed is still owed. If the phrase does the trick, leave it at that, no need to narrate the whole thing.

headings: # When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
## Start With Whatever Showed Up

rows.label: 97.5 A: cut "(if you're in danger, get safe first)"
rows.start: Or if you do get an answer, it could come in different forms

beside.label: Before the cut
beside.text: Or if you do get an answer, it could come in different forms, like as a voice or just a hunch. It's often more like a feeling. Maybe grief or anger. If so just listen and be present for it if that's what it wants. If it tells you to do something, I'd only do it if it's loving and leaves you free. It should make sense, too. Even then, anything big or hard to undo can wait until you're calm and you've checked it against what you actually know (if you're in danger, get safe first).

headings: # When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
## Start With Whatever Showed Up
### When to Change the Strategy

rows.label: 98.7 A: cut "It doesn't have to happen after every session."
rows.start: Sometimes the session itself goes really well. You feel real

beside.label: Before the cut
beside.text: Sometimes the session itself goes really well. You feel real care for your little one and say exactly what they needed to hear. And a few days later you're skipping lunch and saying yes to everything again. A lot of people's first guess is that they didn't go deep enough. I don't think that's it, though, and I don't think this one failed either. Maybe the grown-up just hasn't come out of the exercise with you yet. Whatever you did for your little one in there, I'd try a tiny bit of it out here, like texting a friend that you're having a rough day instead of saying you're fine. That can honestly be harder than the meditation was. One small thing like that can teach your little one more than ten more good meditations. It doesn't have to happen after every session.

headings: # Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy

rows.label: 97.6 A: cut "And yes, those caution signs still count."
rows.start: Remember those guards from The Urge to Escape, above? Same d

beside.label: Before the cut
beside.text: Remember those guards from The Urge to Escape, above? Same deal here, so get enough Nurturer and Protector in the room before you go deep. Borrowed is fine, as long as it’s from someone steady who won’t try to run your trip for you. And yes, those caution signs still count. But feeling attacked by a demon on a psychedelic is not necessarily paranoia. It can be real, and it’s also not bad unless you’re unprepared. It can be supremely empowering when you can send love and see how it fixes the situation.

headings: # Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
## When Escape Leaves Reality Behind

rows.label: 97.7 A: cut "though I don't mean every drug's dangerous for you"
rows.start: Any of those reactions, from mania to paranoia, can also poi

beside.label: Before the cut
beside.text: Any of those reactions, from mania to paranoia, can also point to a vulnerability in you, so I'd be careful with other drugs that mess with what's real too, though I don't mean every drug's dangerous for you. And any predisposition toward mania or psychosis is a warning sign too, whether it's family history, a bad environment or a bad mindset. I can't tell you exactly what to do about it, and nobody can tell you for sure what's best for you. There are just caution signs, and when you see them, you take more precautions of every kind. You have to figure out what they mean for you, and if you can't, get help from trusted advisors.

rows.label: 97.8 A: cut "If you can't tell whether you're safe, I'd treat that as risky."
rows.start: Milder reactions afterward count as caution signs too, like

beside.label: Before the cut
beside.text: Milder reactions afterward count as caution signs too, like getting confused or spaced out (dissociating) again and again. Get professional help right away if any of this is severe or risky, and especially if it keeps going or comes back while you're sober. If you can't tell whether you're safe, I'd treat that as risky. Don't suddenly quit a prescribed medicine, or anything your body is dependent on, just because it might be part of the problem; have a doctor help you stop safely.

headings: # Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy
## Altered States Can Require Reparenting

rows.label: 97.9 A: cut "Know the limit of what you can handle"
rows.start: If a voice or urge is directing you towards harm, and you fe

beside.label: Before the cut
beside.text: If a voice or urge is directing you towards harm, and you feel at risk of acting on it, as with myself and those ghosts at home, move away from that open window and get some outside support. Know the limit of what you can handle, but don't turn it into a prison for life.

headings: # If You Want to Kill Yourself

rows.label: 97.10 A: cut "(and if you're at the edge right now, ...)"
rows.start: But if you're still thinking of staking your life on the opp

beside.label: Before the cut
beside.text: But if you're still thinking of staking your life on the opposite claim, that death is just nothing, look into that claim first (and if you're at the edge right now, the first step above comes before any of this). Researchers at the [University of Virginia](https://med.virginia.edu/perceptual-studies/2025/01/09/uvas-division-of-perceptual-studies-launches-major-research-initiative-on-childrens-past-life-memories/) have been collecting cases of small children who talk about a past life for about sixty years, and there's a big pile of near-death accounts too. I don't think any of it can tell you what dying will be like for you, but I'd read a few of those cases before betting my life on "nothing."

rows.label: 97.11 A: cut "and they can wait until you're calmer"
rows.start: My father used to tell suicidal people, "Oh, you want to kil

beside.label: Before the cut
beside.text: My father used to tell suicidal people, "Oh, you want to kill yourself? That's wonderful. Now you can change what you've always been too afraid to change in your life, and then see if you still want to end it!" His point wasn't that dying is wonderful. If everything's already on the table, what's the change you still can't bring yourself to make? Leaving? Quitting? Moving? Telling your family who you really are? Those aren't free, and you can't always take them back, but they're smaller than dying, and they can wait until you're calmer and have some help. Look at that life you've been afraid to change while you still have a human body.

headings: # Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
## Untangling the Belonging Bargains

rows.label: 98.8 A: cut "That might not be how it goes for everyone"
rows.start: What I found, once I started cultivating my own happiness, w

beside.label: Before the cut
beside.text: What I found, once I started cultivating my own happiness, was that I got a lot better at helping other people toward theirs. That might not be how it goes for everyone, and it doesn't mean unhappy people can't help. Do your part for people who are suffering, and skip the part where you have to be miserable too.

headings: # Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
## Untangling the Belonging Bargains
### Four Pairs That Commonly Hook the Child

rows.label: 96.1 B: your paragraph, word for word
rows.start: Differentiation is slow, and it goes on your whole life.

beside.label: Before
beside.text: Differentiation is slow, and it goes on your whole life. If a family, group or relationship won't let you do this while you're still part of it, temporary distance may be necessary. Some people come back later on different terms. Sometimes the leaving turns out to be permanent, because going back would mean disappearing again. You don't have to know yet which one yours is. As you differentiate, you learn to tell the difference.

headings: # The Inner Guide
## A Belonging Deeper Than Any Group

rows.label: 98.9 A: cut "(that part is optional)"
rows.start: The Guide also points beyond itself, toward a belonging deep

beside.label: Before the cut
beside.text: The Guide also points beyond itself, toward a belonging deeper than any group, one that doesn't ask you to give up being yourself. That might be nature, or existence itself. It might be whatever your tradition sees as ultimate (that part is optional). Love can come from any of these places, and you also belong there, which is a little different. Maybe you've felt that outside somewhere, like you didn't need anybody's okay to be there. The way in is time in nature and contemplative practice, like meditation.

rows.label: 99 A: under the new heading A Belonging Deeper Than Any Group (no word changes)
rows.start: The Guide also points beyond itself, toward a belonging deep

rows.label: 97.12 A: cut "for cult survivors it can be a trigger word"
rows.start: With that under you, belonging with people can get a lot les

beside.label: Before the cut
beside.text: With that under you, belonging with people can get a lot less desperate. Not all at once, but the Guide keeps watching for the moment your little one starts thinking, "If they stop liking me, I won't belong anywhere," and keeps reminding it that a group's approval isn't the deepest belonging there is. By the way, this job doesn't have to be called the Guide. The Wise One works, or your Inner Teacher, and "Guru" does for some people, though for cult survivors it can be a trigger word, which is understandable.

headings: # How Much Happiness Do You Know Is Possible?
## Somatic Heart Opening

rows.label: 97.13 A: cut "It can retraumatize"
rows.start: Rumi says you have to keep breaking your heart until it stay

beside.label: Before the cut
beside.text: Rumi says you have to keep breaking your heart until it stays open. Some people find that deep grieving gives way to warmth, or to feeling connected. Some feel held, in the body. Being loved can open grief, too. Someone takes care of you, and you think, "Why does this make me sad?" It can be sadness for the care that was missing. While you're present and still choosing, stay with it. Crying that deep can overwhelm you, too. It can retraumatize, mostly when nobody's with you or you've disappeared into the sadness. Once it's swamping you instead of opening you, slow down (like turning the song off for the night).

headings: # Borrowed Adulthood in Relationship
## First Social Connections, Done Right

rows.label: 97.14 A: cut "In a real crisis, getting a safe person involved"
rows.start: Then there are people you’re just getting to know. Meeting t

beside.label: Before the cut
beside.text: Then there are people you’re just getting to know. Meeting them can turn into a kind of test--”First impressions are everything,” as they say, but it could be even worse than that, if you need them to prove you’re lovable. Nobody’s a reassurance machine. I’m giving you permission now to quit school and flunk the tests. Get curious about who this person is, and who you are, and let both of you have your own reasons for being there in the beautiful present. Leaning on each other is still a big part of relationships, and it goes both ways. In a real crisis, getting a safe person involved can be exactly the right move.

headings: # Borrowed Adulthood in Relationship
## Speak Toward What You Are Building

rows.label: 98.10 A: cut "(And don't guess it from their gender ...)"
rows.start: What they tell you is worth remembering, too, until they say

beside.label: Before the cut
beside.text: What they tell you is worth remembering, too, until they say something different. (And don't guess it from their gender or some other stereotype.) Same with advice you've already given: if nothing new has changed it, a quick "like I said" and moving on works better than offering it again like it's new.

headings: # When One Life Has Ended and the Next Hasn’t Begun

rows.label: 98.11 A: cut "(I'm only borrowing the word ...)"
rows.start: Your little one can get really loud in the gap after one lif

beside.label: Before the cut
beside.text: Your little one can get really loud in the gap after one life ends and before the next one has formed. A breakup will do it, or moving to another country, an illness, losing your faith or a role, your youngest moving out. Maybe you've left a family or community, maybe you've stayed on new terms. A therapist or helper might step back because you're doing so much better, and suddenly your little one is wailing. For a while the old you is gone and the new you hasn't shown up yet. Tibetan Buddhism calls an in-between state like that a bardo (I'm only borrowing the word, so what it teaches about death and rebirth is up to you).

rows.label: 97.15 A: cut "It doesn't stand in for grieving"
rows.start: All of this happens in you, so it doesn't matter whether the

beside.label: Before the cut
beside.text: All of this happens in you, so it doesn't matter whether they get any of it (nobody's checking their inbox). It doesn't stand in for grieving, though, or for getting in touch when that's right, and your boundaries still apply. Same with the practical stuff. And if it starts making you more compulsive, or a bit unreal, so you can't get back to your life, make it simpler: "I miss you, and I care." Some of that same care can go to the part of you that's still here.
